candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert mixed numbers (and whole numbers when needed) into equivalent improper fractions (or equivalent fractions with a specified denominator) to enable subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three codebooks describe rewriting mixed numbers a b/c as (a·c+b)/c and optionally rewriting whole numbers as fractions to proceed with subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and rewrite each fraction as an equivalent fraction over that denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three codebooks include selecting/finding a common denominator for unlike denominators and scaling fractions to equivalent forms with that denominator.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference of two rational numbers by subtracting numerators once the fractions are expressed with a common (or already-matching) denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A: 'Subtract rational numbers', B: 'Subtract fractions correctly', C: 'Subtract rational numbers' all focus on performing the subtraction step after denominators are compatible, including the same-denominator case.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Express the computed result in simplest accepted form by reducing to lowest terms and/or converting between improper fractions, mixed numbers, and integers when appropriate.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three codebooks include post-subtraction normalization: reducing fractions and optionally rewriting improper fractions as mixed numbers or integers (and noting already-simplest cases).

alignment_summary: Across A, B, and C, the same four-step skill progression appears with only minor naming/wording differences: convert mixed/whole numbers to improper fractions, find a common denominator and rewrite equivalent fractions, subtract with common denominators, and simplify/convert the final result. Every expert skill_id mapped cleanly one-to-one to these four shared concepts.
